findings.issue_text: Permission check in addGuests.handler.ts uses && requiring both isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner, so team admins without owner role get FORBIDDEN even though the UI exposes the action to them (P1)

attendee-add-guests-email.ts and organizer-add-guests-email.ts call renderEmail with template ids never registered in the renderEmail dispatcher mapping, causing email renders to throw or produce empty HTML (P1)
Blacklist and dedupe email comparisons in addGuests.handler.ts are case-sensitive against unnormalized input, allowing blacklist bypass via different casing and duplicate Attendee rows (P2)
addGuests.handler.ts does not check booking.status before mutating, so guests can be added to cancelled/rejected/pending bookings and receive CONFIRMED calendar invites (P2)
EventManager is constructed from ctx.user credentials instead of the booking organizer's credentials, so calendar event attendee updates silently fail when actor is an attendee or team admin (P2)
isInvalidEmail in AddGuestsDialog.tsx is set on validation failure but never reset on dialog close/reopen or success, so the error banner shows on a fresh attempt (P3)
Email send failure in addGuests.handler.ts is swallowed with console.log and the handler returns success, making partial or complete email failures indistinguishable from success (P3)
Team-admin authorization in addGuests.handler.ts uses && instead of ||, requiring both admin AND owner, denying non-owner team admins (P1)

Blacklisted/already-attendee emails are silently dropped; handler returns success with no indication that emails were discarded, and all-filtered case throws misleading BAD_REQUEST message (P2)
No case-insensitive dedup against existing attendees: duplicate attendee rows, duplicate calendar/email sends, and double seat consumption possible (P2)
Seat-based event types accepted but unhandled: no seat-availability check, no BookingSeat creation, no capacity enforcement, allowing overbooking and seat state desync (P1)

Email send failures swallowed with console.log discarding err entirely, leaving no diagnostic trail for failed invitations (P3)
Authorization uses && instead of || in isTeamAdminOrOwner at addGuests.handler.ts:55-57, making team admins unable to add guests (only team owners pass)

Calendar update at addGuests.handler.ts:141-146 uses the acting user's credentials instead of the booking owner's, so an attendee can trigger calendar updates against the organizer's calendar with the wrong credential set
No rollback of prisma.booking.update when the calendar update fails, causing DB and calendar event to permanently diverge
Seat-capacity invariant not enforced for seated event types: addGuests handler reads seatsPerTimeSlot but performs a raw createMany with no capacity check and no bookingSeat creation

Add guests action in BookingListItem.tsx:193-199 is offered with no booking-status filter, allowing guests to be added to cancelled or rejected bookings and sending ICS with status CONFIRMED for dead meetings

Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive on the guest side at addGuests.handler.ts:66-72: the blacklist is lowercased but guest emails are not, so capitalization variations bypass the blacklist

Existing-attendee dedup uses exact === comparison and the client-side uniqueness check in AddGuestsDialog.tsx is case-sensitive, allowing duplicate attendee rows and duplicate ICS entries for the same mailbox with different casing

Guests array in addGuests.schema.ts:5 has no .max() bound, allowing any authorized user to submit thousands of emails in one mutation causing mass attendee inserts, emails, and a massive calendar-update call

addGuests.handler.ts — The handler's createMany inserts duplicate guest emails verbatim; uniqueGuests filter only dedups against pre-existing attendees, not within the guests input array

addGuests.handler.ts:57-78 — Check-then-insert TOCTOU race: two concurrent requests for the same guest both pass the attendee check and both insert, since no unique constraint on BookingAttendee(bookingId, email) is enforced
addGuests.handler.ts:53-56 — Case-sensitive duplicate-attendee check lets re-adding 'Foo@X.com' when 'foo@x.com' already attends create a duplicate attendee
addGuests.handler.ts:53-56, 63-68 — Guests are never lowercased while the blacklist is, so blacklist is bypassed by case variation (e.g., 'Spam@x.com' passes while 'spam@x.com' is blocked)
addGuests.handler.ts:150-155 — Calendar update runs with the caller's (possibly an attendee's) credentials instead of the organizer's, causing failures or updates against the wrong calendar

addGuests.handler.ts:75-82, 149-174 — Multi-step write has no transaction/compensation: attendee rows commit first, then a calendar-update failure persists guests while the calendar/ICS is never updated
addGuests.handler.ts — Retry after a calendar failure is a trap: retrying with the same emails hits uniqueGuests.length === 0 and returns a misleading 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' BAD_REQUEST

addGuests.schema.ts:4: Server schema lacks email uniqueness refine that exists in client schema, allowing API callers to submit duplicate emails that get inserted as duplicate attendee rows (client AddGuestsDialog.tsx:27-31 has the refine)

addGuests.handler.ts:61-73: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS check is case-sensitive — blacklist emails are lowercased but the guest email is not, so case-variant emails bypass the blacklist and duplicate existing attendees (also affects email-manager.ts:537 newGuests.includes(attendee.email) template selection)

AddGuestsDialog.tsx:60-70 + addGuests.handler.ts:66-72: Handler silently drops blacklisted or already-attending guests but UI shows 'Guests added' success toast for the full input, giving no indication which guests were filtered out

addGuests.handler.ts:47-58, 155-163: Attendee write-permission grant is over-granted with no attendee-facing UI, and EventManager is constructed with the actor's (attendee's) credentials rather than the organizer's, so calendar updates use credentials that don't own the event
Blacklist check in addGuests.handler.ts:52-56 is case-bypassable: blacklist emails are lowercased but the incoming guest email is not, so banned guests can be added by changing casing
Same case-sensitivity flaw affects the existing-attendee dedupe (guest === attendee.email at line 59), allowing case-variant duplicates of existing attendees

addGuests.schema.ts:4 has an unbounded guests array (no .max()), allowing a single request to create thousands of attendees and fan out mass emails/ICS invites, enabling email-bombing and calendar rate-limit burn
addGuests.handler.ts:47-52 grants mutation rights to mere attendees, who can inject guests and trigger email sends (including meeting links) on the organizer's booking
Calendar update in the attendee path runs with the caller's credentials (getUsersCredentials) instead of the organizer's, attempting a calendar mutation with credentials that don't own the event
addGuests.handler.ts:172 swallows email-send failures with a bare console.log, returning success to the caller and masking partial-send state so users may not receive the meeting link
Missing test coverage for the new addGuests mutation, including authz branching, guest dedup/blacklist filtering, and email routing in sendAddGuestsEmails
Missing E2E test coverage despite the diff adding data-testid attributes (add_members, add-another-email, add-emails) that imply E2E tests were intended

No server-side uniqueness enforcement within the guests array: ZAddGuestsInputSchema accepts duplicates and the uniqueGuests filter only dedupes against existing attendees, so duplicate emails insert duplicate Attendee rows via createMany

Dedup against existing attendees is case-sensitive (guest === attendee.email) while blacklist comparison lowercases input, allowing case-variant duplicates to be added and silently bypassing BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS for non-lowercase input

Non-transactional multi-step write: prisma.booking.update persists attendees before updateCalendarAttendees and sendAddGuestsEmails, and email failures are swallowed, leaving DB attendees out of sync with calendar and emails with no rollback

New attendees are created on booking.attendees without seat records or capacity checks for seated bookings (booking.eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot is read but unaccounted), causing inconsistent seat accounting
Append-only attendee writes with no delete-guests endpoint in the diff means any bad attendee rows cannot be removed by the feature

adjudication_records.issue_text: Permission check in addGuests.handler.ts uses && requiring both isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner, so team admins without owner role get FORBIDDEN even though the UI exposes the action to them (P1)

attendee-add-guests-email.ts and organizer-add-guests-email.ts call renderEmail with template ids never registered in the renderEmail dispatcher mapping, causing email renders to throw or produce empty HTML (P1)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows both email classes calling `renderEmail("AttendeeAddGuestsEmail", ...)` / `renderEmail("OrganizerAddGuestsEmail", ...)`, and it also adds matching React templates under `packages/emails/src/templates/{AttendeeAddGuestsEmail,OrganizerAddGuestsEmail}.tsx` and exports them in `packages/emails/src/templates/index.ts`. Since the supposed “renderEmail dispatcher mapping” is not shown in the diff, and the diff *does* include the typical registration point (exporting from `src/templates/index.ts`), there’s no verifiable evidence here that these template IDs are unregistered or would render empty/throw.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklist and dedupe email comparisons in addGuests.handler.ts are case-sensitive against unnormalized input, allowing blacklist bypass via different casing and duplicate Attendee rows (P2)
addGuests.handler.ts does not check booking.status before mutating, so guests can be added to cancelled/rejected/pending bookings and receive CONFIRMED calendar invites (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler fetches the booking and unconditionally updates `attendees` via `prisma.booking.update(...)` with `createMany`, without checking any `booking.status`/cancellation state before mutating. It then builds a `CalendarEvent` and calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`. The new email templates generate ICS payloads with `status: "CONFIRMED"` (see `packages/emails/templates/*add-guests-email.ts`). Since there is no status gate in the handler, this diff allows adding guests (and sending CONFIRMED invites/emails) even if the booking is cancelled/rejected/pending, assuming those states exist on the booking model.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager is constructed from ctx.user credentials instead of the booking organizer's credentials, so calendar event attendee updates silently fail when actor is an attendee or team admin (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the booking organizer can differ from the actor (`ctx.user`) because the mutation allows team admins/owners and attendees to add guests. However, the code builds the `EventManager` using `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })`, i.e., the actor’s credentials, not the booking organizer’s. The diff even loads `booking.user.credentials` via the initial `prisma.booking.findFirst({ include: { user: { include: { credentials: true }}}})` but never uses it. Since `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` is meant to update the booking’s calendar event, using a non-organizer’s credentials is a concrete correctness issue that can prevent the update when the actor isn’t the organizer.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isInvalidEmail in AddGuestsDialog.tsx is set on validation failure but never reset on dialog close/reopen or success, so the error banner shows on a fresh attempt (P3)

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when Zod validation fails in `handleAdd`, but it is only reset to `false` in the Cancel button handler. When the dialog is closed via `onOpenChange` (e.g., clicking outside/ESC) it calls `setIsOpenDialog` directly and does not reset `isInvalidEmail`. Also, the `onSuccess` handler closes the dialog and resets `multiEmailValue` but does not reset `isInvalidEmail`. Therefore reopening the dialog after a validation failure (or after a success that followed a previous failure) can show the error banner on a fresh attempt.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email send failure in addGuests.handler.ts is swallowed with console.log and the handler returns success, making partial or complete email failures indistinguishable from success (P3)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the email send is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` and the error is neither rethrown nor returned. The handler then proceeds to return `{ message: "Guests added" }` regardless of whether all/some/no emails were sent, making email-delivery failures indistinguishable from success and also dropping the error details (only a generic console.log).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Team-admin authorization in addGuests.handler.ts uses && instead of ||, requiring both admin AND owner, denying non-owner team admins (P1)
matched_golden_ids: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same permission logic bug: using && between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner incorrectly requires both to be true, and it should be || so either role grants access.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No booking status check in addGuests.handler.ts: guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, or pending bookings, resurrecting cancelled meetings (P1)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler fetches the booking by `id` and only checks authorization (team admin/owner, organizer, or attendee) and that there is at least one non-blacklisted, non-duplicate guest. It then updates the booking’s `attendees`, calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, and sends emails/ICS with `status: "CONFIRMED"` via `sendAddGuestsEmails`, without any check of the booking’s status (e.g., cancelled/rejected/pending). Therefore, as implemented in the diff, guests can be added regardless of booking status, and calendar/email side effects will still occur.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklist check in addGuests.handler.ts is case-sensitive while blacklist entries are lowercased, allowing trivial bypass via case variation (P1)
Blacklisted/already-attendee emails are silently dropped; handler returns success with no indication that emails were discarded, and all-filtered case throws misleading BAD_REQUEST message (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the handler filters the requested `guests` into `uniqueGuests` by dropping emails that are already in `booking.attendees` or are in `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`. It then proceeds to add only `uniqueGuests` but returns a generic success `{ message: "Guests added" }` without reporting which emails were skipped, so some inputs can be silently discarded. If all provided emails are filtered out, it throws `TRPCError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST", message: "emails_must_be_unique_valid" })`, but that message is misleading because the failure can be due to "already an attendee" or "blacklisted" rather than invalid/non-unique formatting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No case-insensitive dedup against existing attendees: duplicate attendee rows, duplicate calendar/email sends, and double seat consumption possible (P2)

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: deduping is strictly case-sensitive. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` filters out existing attendees with `guest === attendee.email` and checks blacklist with `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` where the blacklist is lowercased but `guest` is not. The client-side dialog also enforces uniqueness via `new Set(emails)` which is also case-sensitive. So entering `Foo@bar.com` when `foo@bar.com` already exists (or duplicating with different casing) will pass and can create duplicate attendee rows and trigger downstream `updateCalendarAttendees`/email logic with duplicates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Seat-based event types accepted but unhandled: no seat-availability check, no BookingSeat creation, no capacity enforcement, allowing overbooking and seat state desync (P1)

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` blindly appends new `booking.attendees` via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` and then updates calendars/emails. It never checks `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` (seat-based/capacity settings are explicitly carried into the `CalendarEvent`), nor does it perform any capacity/seat-availability enforcement before adding attendees. Nothing in the diff creates/updates any seat-specific record (e.g., a `BookingSeat`-like entity) or otherwise reconciles seat counts, so for seat-based event types this endpoint can add more attendees than allowed and potentially desync whatever seat/capacity model exists elsewhere.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager built from ctx.user instead of booking owner: calendar update fails or hits wrong calendar when actor differs from organizer, causing DB/calendar/email divergence (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler`, the mutation explicitly allows non-organizers to add guests (`isTeamAdminOrOwner` OR `isOrganizer` OR `isAttendee`). However the calendar sync is performed via `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })` where `user`/`credentials` come from `ctx.user` (the actor), not from the booking owner/organizer (`booking.userId` / `organizer`). If an attendee (or team admin) triggers this, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will attempt to update the calendar using the actor’s credentials rather than the organizer’s, which can fail (no matching calendar integration) or update the wrong external calendar, while the DB attendees were already updated (`prisma.booking.update`). That creates a verifiable risk of DB ↔ external calendar divergence introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email send failures swallowed with console.log discarding err entirely, leaving no diagnostic trail for failed invitations (P3)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the call to `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is wrapped in a `try/catch` that only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and does not log or otherwise surface the caught `err` (nor rethrow/return an error). This means email send failures are effectively swallowed with no actionable diagnostics about the underlying failure cause, matching the proposed finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization uses && instead of || in isTeamAdminOrOwner at addGuests.handler.ts:55-57, making team admins unable to add guests (only team owners pass)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. This requires the user to be BOTH a team admin and a team owner to pass that check. The variable name and intended permission (“admin or owner”) implies it should be `||`, otherwise a team admin who is not also an owner will fail authorization and be blocked from adding guests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Calendar update at addGuests.handler.ts:141-146 uses the acting user's credentials instead of the booking owner's, so an attendee can trigger calendar updates against the organizer's calendar with the wrong credential set

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the mutation allows an attendee (isAttendee) to add guests. However, the calendar update path builds the EventManager using the acting session user (`const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })`), not the booking owner/organizer. Since the calendar event `evt` is clearly constructed around the booking/organizer (organizer fields, destinationCalendar from booking/user, etc.), using the attendee’s credentials means the subsequent `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will run with the wrong credential set whenever the caller isn’t the organizer. This is a real correctness defect introduced/visible in the diff (calendar updates may fail or update the wrong account), even if the finding’s security framing is a bit overstated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No rollback of prisma.booking.update when the calendar update fails, causing DB and calendar event to permanently diverge

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the code first persists new attendees via prisma.booking.update(...attendees.createMany...). After that it calls eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking) to sync the external calendar, but this call is not wrapped in a transaction with the DB update and is not caught/compensated. If updateCalendarAttendees throws (e.g., external calendar API failure), the handler will error after the DB write has already succeeded, leaving booking.attendees updated in the database while the calendar event may remain unchanged (divergence). There is also no rollback/compensating delete of the newly created attendees.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Seat-capacity invariant not enforced for seated event types: addGuests handler reads seatsPerTimeSlot but performs a raw createMany with no capacity check and no bookingSeat creation

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` updates `booking.attendees` via `createMany` with the provided guest emails and does not check `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` (or any other capacity constraint) against the current attendee count before inserting. The handler even propagates `seatsPerTimeSlot`/`seatsShowAttendees` into the `CalendarEvent` object, but never enforces them, so for seated/capacity-limited event types this endpoint can add attendees beyond the seat limit (a correctness/invariant violation introduced by this diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Add guests action in BookingListItem.tsx:193-199 is offered with no booking-status filter, allowing guests to be added to cancelled or rejected bookings and sending ICS with status CONFIRMED for dead meetings

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an unconditional "additional_guests" action to the BookingListItem menu (no condition on any booking status/state in the added block), and the new `addGuestsHandler` similarly does not check any booking lifecycle/status before mutating attendees and sending emails. The new add-guests email templates always generate ICS with `status: "CONFIRMED"` (`generateIcsString({ ..., status: "CONFIRMED" })`). Given the existing codebase clearly supports cancellations (there are multiple cancelled email templates imported), adding guests to a cancelled/rejected booking would still proceed and send a CONFIRMED ICS, which is a correctness defect introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive on the guest side at addGuests.handler.ts:66-72: the blacklist is lowercased but guest emails are not, so capitalization variations bypass the blacklist

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In addGuests.handler.ts the blacklist is normalized to lowercase (`BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.split(...).map(email => email.toLowerCase())`), but the incoming `guests` values are used as-is when filtering (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`). Since `z.string().email()` does not lowercase, a guest email like `Blocked@Example.com` would not match a blacklist entry `blocked@example.com` and would bypass the blacklist. The same case-sensitive equality is also used against existing attendees (`guest === attendee.email`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Existing-attendee dedup uses exact === comparison and the client-side uniqueness check in AddGuestsDialog.tsx is case-sensitive, allowing duplicate attendee rows and duplicate ICS entries for the same mailbox with different casing

Email failure is silently swallowed at addGuests.handler.ts:170-173 with a bare console.log (no error object, no log level), and the handler returns success regardless, telling the user guests were added when emails may not have been sent

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the call to `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is wrapped in a `try/catch` that only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and does not log the caught `err` or rethrow/return an error. Immediately after, the handler returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` regardless of whether email sending failed. This means email delivery failures are silently ignored (poor observability) and the API response indicates success even if that side effect (sending emails) did not complete.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Guests array in addGuests.schema.ts:5 has no .max() bound, allowing any authorized user to submit thousands of emails in one mutation causing mass attendee inserts, emails, and a massive calendar-update call

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts`, `guests` is defined as `z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max()`/size constraint. The new mutation `addGuests` (`_router.tsx` + `addGuests.handler.ts`) uses that array directly to (1) `createMany` attendee rows (`guestsFullDetails`), (2) call `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, and (3) send emails in bulk via `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`. Since authorization includes any attendee (`isAttendee`) as well as organizer/admin, an authorized user can submit an extremely large `guests` array, causing large DB writes and expensive downstream calendar/email work. No other limiting logic is present in the diff (only a `uniqueGuests.length === 0` check), so the finding is verifiably applicable to this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isInvalidEmail validation state in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:22,49-51 is sticky and never cleared on retry, so the invalid-email warning remains visible even after the mutation succeeds with valid input

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when `safeParse` fails, but it is never set back to `false` in the success path (neither when validation passes nor in the mutation `onSuccess`). The only resets are in the Cancel button handler. As a result, after a user fixes the emails and retries, the warning will remain visible while submitting; and if the dialog is closed/reopened (including after a successful mutation, which closes the dialog), `isInvalidEmail` can still be `true`, so the warning will show even with fresh/empty inputs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:44-47 — Permission gate uses `&&` instead of `||`, so team admins who aren't owners are denied (FORBIDDEN), contradicting the 'AdminOrOwner' intent

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the variable `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner. Given the name/intent "AdminOrOwner", this is a logic bug: a team admin who is not also an owner will have `isTeamAdminOrOwner === false` and can be denied by the subsequent permission check `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN;`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:44-47 — Fallback `?? 0` runs two pointless DB-backed isTeamAdmin/isTeamOwner checks against nonexistent team id 0 on every personal-booking call

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed unconditionally as `(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) && (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0))`. When the booking is not team-based (`booking.eventType?.teamId` is `undefined`/`null`), the `?? 0` fallback causes both `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` to run using teamId `0`, resulting in two unnecessary DB-backed permission checks for non-team (personal) bookings. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.schema.ts:3-6 — Guest uniqueness is validated only in the client AddGuestsDialog component, not in the shared server schema, so non-UI callers can submit duplicate guests
addGuests.handler.ts — The handler's createMany inserts duplicate guest emails verbatim; uniqueGuests filter only dedups against pre-existing attendees, not within the guests input array
matched_golden_ids: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate states that createMany will insert duplicate guest emails because uniqueGuests only filters against existing attendees (and implicitly blacklists) but does not deduplicate within the input guests array. This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:57-78 — Check-then-insert TOCTOU race: two concurrent requests for the same guest both pass the attendee check and both insert, since no unique constraint on BookingAttendee(bookingId, email) is enforced

adjudication.rationale: The handler does perform a check-then-insert pattern: it reads existing attendees (`booking.attendees`) and then later does `booking.update` with `attendees.createMany` based on that earlier snapshot. However, the proposed finding’s key claim—“since no unique constraint on BookingAttendee(bookingId, email) is enforced” and therefore “both insert”—is not verifiable from this diff (no Prisma schema/migration showing constraints is included). If a DB unique constraint exists, the second concurrent insert would fail rather than create duplicates. The diff alone only shows a potential race window, not that duplicates can actually be inserted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:53-56 — Case-sensitive duplicate-attendee check lets re-adding 'Foo@X.com' when 'foo@x.com' already attends create a duplicate attendee

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the duplicate filter uses a case-sensitive comparison: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`. Neither `guest` nor `attendee.email` is normalized (e.g., `.toLowerCase()`), while the blacklist is lowercased but `guest` is not, indicating inconsistent casing handling. As a result, if an existing attendee email is stored as `foo@x.com`, providing `Foo@x.com` will not be detected as a duplicate and will be included in `uniqueGuests`, allowing creation of a logically-duplicate attendee record.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:53-56, 63-68 — Guests are never lowercased while the blacklist is, so blacklist is bypassed by case variation (e.g., 'Spam@x.com' passes while 'spam@x.com' is blocked)
addGuests.handler.ts:150-155 — Calendar update runs with the caller's (possibly an attendee's) credentials instead of the organizer's, causing failures or updates against the wrong calendar

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the mutation explicitly allows an attendee to call it (`isAttendee` check), but the calendar update is performed using the caller's session user: `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })`. The organizer data is fetched separately (`organizer = await prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow(...)`) and used to build `evt.organizer`, but those organizer credentials are never used for `updateCalendarAttendees`. This makes the calendar sync dependent on (and potentially applied under) the attendee's credentials rather than the booking organizer's, which can cause failures (attendee has no calendar credentials) or incorrect target calendar updates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:75-82, 149-174 — Multi-step write has no transaction/compensation: attendee rows commit first, then a calendar-update failure persists guests while the calendar/ICS is never updated

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the code first persists new attendees via prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany }}}) and only afterwards calls eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking), which can fail/throw (it updates external calendar state). There is no surrounding transaction and no rollback/compensation logic if the calendar update fails, so the DB change (new guest attendee rows) can be committed while the calendar/ICS update does not happen and the mutation may error out. This is a real inconsistency risk introduced by the multi-step write sequence shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts — Retry after a calendar failure is a trap: retrying with the same emails hits uniqueGuests.length === 0 and returns a misleading 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' BAD_REQUEST

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In addGuests.handler.ts the DB update (prisma.booking.update creating attendees) happens *before* eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking). If updateCalendarAttendees throws, the mutation fails but the new guests are already persisted. A user retrying the same request will refetch the booking (now containing those emails), compute uniqueGuests by filtering out existing attendees, get uniqueGuests.length === 0, and throw BAD_REQUEST with message "emails_must_be_unique_valid"—misleading because the real issue on the first attempt was the calendar update failure (partial success).

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts — Email error handling logs only a static message via console.log with no error object, stack, or telemetry, making silent notification loss undiagnosable

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the email sending is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }`. The caught `err` is not logged or reported (no error object/stack), and the error is swallowed (no rethrow/return error), so failures to send notification emails become effectively silent and hard to diagnose. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.schema.ts:4 — Unbounded guest array (no .max()) allows thousands of addresses in one request, causing an unbounded createMany and unbounded synchronous Promise.all email fanout

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts`, `guests` is defined as `z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max()`, so a client can submit an extremely large list. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, this list is used to build `guestsFullDetails` and passed to Prisma `attendees.createMany` (unbounded write), and then `sendAddGuestsEmails` is called which builds an `emailsToSend` array including a per-attendee `sendEmail(...)` and awaits `Promise.all(emailsToSend)` (unbounded email fanout/concurrency). This is a concrete, verifiable resource-exhaustion risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:110-113 — For seated event types, the handler reads seatsPerTimeSlot but neither enforces capacity nor creates BookingSeat records, so added guests can exceed seatsPerTimeSlot and are invisible to the seating data model

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the code does include `seatsPerTimeSlot`/`seatsShowAttendees` on the constructed `CalendarEvent`, but it does not perform any capacity check. However, the finding’s stronger claim—"for seated event types" it must enforce `seatsPerTimeSlot` and "create BookingSeat records"—is not verifiable from this diff: there is no `BookingSeat` model/relationship shown, and nothing in the diff establishes that adding `booking.attendees` is the wrong persistence mechanism for seated events or that `seatsPerTimeSlot` should be enforced during a guest-add operation. That part is speculative about data model/business rules outside the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:43-45: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, requiring users to be both admin AND owner (collapsing to owner-only), silently forbidding team admins the permission model should allow

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. This requires the user to satisfy *both* predicates. Given the variable name (`isTeamAdminOrOwner`) and the later permission gate `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) ...`, this logic will deny access to a user who is a team admin but not a team owner (and vice versa), which is very likely unintended and is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.schema.ts:4: Server schema lacks email uniqueness refine that exists in client schema, allowing API callers to submit duplicate emails that get inserted as duplicate attendee rows (client AddGuestsDialog.tsx:27-31 has the refine)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.schema.ts` the server accepts `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness constraint. The handler (`addGuests.handler.ts`) also does not dedupe `guests`—it filters only against existing booking attendees and a blacklist, so duplicates within the submitted `guests` array will remain in `uniqueGuests` and be passed to `attendees.createMany`. This can lead to duplicate attendee rows being inserted (or a DB error if a unique constraint exists), whereas the client-side dialog explicitly refines for uniqueness.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:61-73: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS check is case-sensitive — blacklist emails are lowercased but the guest email is not, so case-variant emails bypass the blacklist and duplicate existing attendees (also affects email-manager.ts:537 newGuests.includes(attendee.email) template selection)

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the blacklist is normalized to lowercase (`.map(...toLowerCase())`), but the incoming `guest` string is compared without normalization: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. This makes the blacklist check case-sensitive and allows bypass via case-variant emails (e.g., `Test@x.com` vs `test@x.com`). Similarly, the duplicate-attendee check uses `guest === attendee.email` without case normalization, so case variants can slip through. In email-manager.ts, `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` is also case-sensitive, so case differences between stored attendee emails and the `newGuests` array can cause incorrect template selection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog.tsx:60-70 + addGuests.handler.ts:66-72: Handler silently drops blacklisted or already-attending guests but UI shows 'Guests added' success toast for the full input, giving no indication which guests were filtered out

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog, onSuccess always shows a generic `showToast(t("guests_added"), "success")` after calling `addGuestsMutation.mutate({ bookingId, guests: multiEmailValue })`, with no reconciliation against what was actually added. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the server computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering out emails that are already in `booking.attendees` and any `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`, and then only creates attendees for `uniqueGuests`. If the user submitted a mix of valid+filtered emails, the mutation still succeeds and returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` without indicating which inputs were dropped. This can mislead the UI into implying all provided guests were added when some were silently ignored.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:47-58, 155-163: Attendee write-permission grant is over-granted with no attendee-facing UI, and EventManager is constructed with the actor's (attendee's) credentials rather than the organizer's, so calendar updates use credentials that don't own the event

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the mutation explicitly grants write access to any booking attendee: `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` and then allows the operation when `isAttendee` is true (lines ~47-58). That means an attendee can add arbitrary guest emails and trigger side effects (DB writes + email sends + calendar updates) even though the only UI added in this diff is in BookingListItem (organizer-side), making the permission expansion plausibly unintended. Additionally, the calendar update uses credentials of the *actor* (`getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })`, lines ~155-163) rather than the organizer/booking owner whose calendar event is being updated; the handler even loads `booking.user.credentials` earlier but never uses them. If an attendee triggers this mutation, calendar updates will run with credentials that likely do not own the event, causing incorrect behavior or failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklist check in addGuests.handler.ts:52-56 is case-bypassable: blacklist emails are lowercased but the incoming guest email is not, so banned guests can be added by changing casing
matched_golden_ids: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same flaw: the blacklist is normalized to lowercase but the guest email being checked is not, so the includes() check can be bypassed by using uppercase/mixed-case emails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Same case-sensitivity flaw affects the existing-attendee dedupe (guest === attendee.email at line 59), allowing case-variant duplicates of existing attendees

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is computed with `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`. This strict equality check is case-sensitive and `guest` is not normalized (e.g., lowercased) before comparison. Therefore, if an existing attendee email is stored as `test@example.com`, submitting `Test@example.com` would bypass the dedupe check and be treated as a new guest, allowing case-variant duplicates to be added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.schema.ts:4 has an unbounded guests array (no .max()), allowing a single request to create thousands of attendees and fan out mass emails/ICS invites, enabling email-bombing and calendar rate-limit burn

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts`, `guests` is defined as `z.array(z.string().email())` with no upper bound. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, those emails are used to `createMany` new attendee records and then `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` which fans out emails/ICS invites across attendees (and organizer/team members). Because the endpoint is an `authedProcedure` and even an existing attendee is authorized (`isAttendee`), a single authenticated request can include an extremely large `guests` array and trigger large DB writes + calendar updates + mass outbound email, making email/calendar abuse feasible.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:47-52 grants mutation rights to mere attendees, who can inject guests and trigger email sends (including meeting links) on the organizer's booking

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, authorization explicitly allows any attendee to perform the mutation: `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` and the guard only blocks if `!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee`. That means a non-organizer attendee can add arbitrary guest emails to the booking (`prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`), then the server updates calendar attendees via `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` (using the organizer’s credentials) and sends emails via `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, which can include event details/meeting links. This matches the proposed finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Calendar update in the attendee path runs with the caller's credentials (getUsersCredentials) instead of the organizer's, attempting a calendar mutation with credentials that don't own the event

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation is allowed for non-organizers (`isAttendee` path). Regardless of who calls it, the calendar update is executed with `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })`, where `user` is the caller (`ctx.user`). For an attendee caller, these credentials are not the organizer’s (or event owner’s) calendar credentials, yet `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` attempts to mutate the booking’s calendar event. The diff even fetches `booking.user` including `credentials`, but does not use them, reinforcing that organizer credentials were likely intended. This makes the finding a real correctness issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:172 swallows email-send failures with a bare console.log, returning success to the caller and masking partial-send state so users may not receive the meeting link

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts` the call to `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is wrapped in a `try/catch` that only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and then continues to return `{ message: "Guests added" }`. This means any failure to send notification/ICS emails is silently ignored and the client will still see a successful mutation (`onSuccess` toast/close), masking the fact that guests/organizers may not receive the email updates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing test coverage for the new addGuests mutation, including authz branching, guest dedup/blacklist filtering, and email routing in sendAddGuestsEmails

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new UI (AddGuestsDialog), a new TRPC mutation (viewer.bookings.addGuests), and new email-sending logic (sendAddGuestsEmails), but it does not add or modify any test files. While that makes it reasonable to *suggest* adding tests, “missing test coverage” is not a concrete, verifiable defect in the code itself from this diff alone (no failing behavior or explicit project requirement shown). The finding is process-oriented rather than identifying an actual bug/security/correctness issue in the implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing E2E test coverage despite the diff adding data-testid attributes (add_members, add-another-email, add-emails) that imply E2E tests were intended

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new UI and data-testid attributes, but it does not include or reference any test suite, test requirements, or removed tests. Concluding that E2E tests are “missing” because data-testid exists is speculative and not a verifiable defect in the code change itself; data-testid can be used for unit/integration tests or future-proofing and its presence does not imply an intended but absent E2E test in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No server-side uniqueness enforcement within the guests array: ZAddGuestsInputSchema accepts duplicates and the uniqueGuests filter only dedupes against existing attendees, so duplicate emails insert duplicate Attendee rows via createMany

adjudication.rationale: The server-side schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only validates `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` (no uniqueness refinement). In `addGuestsHandler`, `uniqueGuests` is computed by filtering only against `booking.attendees` and a blacklist, but it does not deduplicate duplicates within the incoming `guests` array itself. Because `booking.attendees` is the pre-update list, an input like `["a@example.com","a@example.com"]` will keep both entries in `uniqueGuests`, producing duplicate rows in `guestsFullDetails`, and `attendees.createMany({ data: guestsFullDetails })` will attempt to insert duplicates (either creating duplicate attendee rows or causing a DB constraint error, depending on schema). This is a real correctness problem introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dedup against existing attendees is case-sensitive (guest === attendee.email) while blacklist comparison lowercases input, allowing case-variant duplicates to be added and silently bypassing BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS for non-lowercase input

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, deduplication uses strict equality against existing attendees: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`, which is case-sensitive. The blacklist is normalized to lowercase (`.map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`) but the input `guest` is not lowercased before `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`, so case-variant inputs (e.g. `Bad@Example.com`) can bypass a lowercased blacklist entry and also be treated as “new” even if `bad@example.com` is already an attendee. Zod `z.string().email()` validates format but does not normalize case, so this issue is verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-transactional multi-step write: prisma.booking.update persists attendees before updateCalendarAttendees and sendAddGuestsEmails, and email failures are swallowed, leaving DB attendees out of sync with calendar and emails with no rollback

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the code first persists new attendees via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and only afterwards performs external side effects: `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and then `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`. There is no database transaction tying the attendee write to the calendar update/email sending, so if `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the mutation fails but the DB change has already been committed, leaving attendees potentially out of sync with the calendar. Additionally, email sending errors are explicitly swallowed in a try/catch (only `console.log`), so the DB/calendar can be updated while emails are not sent, with no rollback or error surfaced to the caller.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New attendees are created on booking.attendees without seat records or capacity checks for seated bookings (booking.eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot is read but unaccounted), causing inconsistent seat accounting

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the mutation unconditionally creates new booking.attendees via prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}}) after only filtering duplicates/blacklist. Although it reads booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot (and seatsShowAttendees) when constructing the CalendarEvent, it never enforces any capacity/seat limit before adding attendees. For seat-based ("seated") event types, this can allow adding more attendees than allowed, leading to incorrect seat/capacity accounting. The absence of any capacity check is directly verifiable in the diff; whether there is a separate "seat record" table is not shown here, but the core issue (no seatsPerTimeSlot enforcement) is real.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Append-only attendee writes with no delete-guests endpoint in the diff means any bad attendee rows cannot be removed by the feature

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce an `addGuests` mutation that only appends attendees via `attendees.createMany` and does not include any corresponding “remove guests”/delete logic in the new handler/router/UI. However, the proposed finding claims this means attendee rows “cannot be removed by the feature,” which is not verifiable from the diff: (1) the new feature may be intentionally add-only, and (2) deletion/editing of attendees could exist elsewhere in the codebase outside this diff. Therefore this is a product/feature gap speculation rather than a concrete defect introduced by the shown changes.
